# Mesh & vertical grid {.unnumbered}

*This chapter describes the horizontal mesh and the vertical coordinate, and
illustrates the wet–dry behaviour of the shallow upper river.*

The mesh is the geometric backbone of the model. `hgrid.gr3` (and its lon-lat
twin `hgrid.ll`) define the node coordinates, depths and element connectivity;
`vgrid.in` sets the vertical coordinate. Every other input and output is indexed
off this mesh.

::: {.callout-note}
The detailed mesh-generation methodology and the per-node `*.gr3` spatial fields
are still to be documented here — see the planned content below.
:::

## Wet and dry in the upper river

A practical consequence of the bathymetry shows up at the head of the estuary:
the upper river is shallow and intermittently dry, so the wet channel narrows
and widens over the tidal cycle. This matters for the model because the river
point source discharges into cells that may be dry or near-dry — the cause of
the source-injection issue examined in the
[conservation testing](../part4-nutrient-budget/16-conservation-testing.qmd).

![Upper-river bathymetry and wet/dry connectivity. Source: `analytics/pioneer_region_flux/archive/upper_river_connectivity.py`](../../assets/images/setup/upper_river_connectivity.png){#fig-connectivity}
